name: Congenital Diaphragmatic Hernia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Prenatal and postnatal imaging diagnostic criteria for CDH

criteria.description: Presence of a defect in the diaphragm allowing abdominal viscera to herniate into the thoracic cavity
Evidence of pulmonary hypoplasia on imaging or clinical examination
Mediastinal shift visible on prenatal ultrasound or postnatal chest X-ray

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Identification of a diaphragmatic defect with herniation of abdominal contents into the thoracic cavity on imaging
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is often made prenatally via ultrasound or postnatally by chest radiography and confirmed by surgical findings.

laboratory: Arterial blood gas showing hypoxemia and respiratory acidosis
Elevated lactate in severe cases due to hypoxia
imaging: Prenatal ultrasound showing herniation of abdominal contents into thorax
Chest X-ray demonstrating bowel loops in thoracic cavity and mediastinal shift
other: Echocardiography to assess pulmonary hypertension and cardiac anomalies

distinguishingFeatures: Elevated but intact diaphragm on imaging
Overinflated lung lobe without abdominal organ displacement

redFlags: Severe respiratory distress unresponsive to oxygen therapy
Persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn
Failure to establish adequate ventilation after birth
references: Pober BR. Overview of epidemiology, genetics, clinical presentation, and diagnosis of congenital diaphragmatic hernia. UpToDate. 2024.
The Congenital Diaphragmatic Hernia Study Group. Congenital diaphragmatic hernia: current management and outcomes. Semin Perinatol. 2023.
Orphanet Report Series: Congenital diaphragmatic hernia. Orphanet. 2024.
